President Trump hosted executives from several major technology companies on Tuesday, pushing forward an agreement that essentially allows the artificial intelligence industry to self-regulate.

Trump signed the "White House Super-Intelligence Agreement" with these tech executives, with so-called "super-intelligence" being the president's preferred term to replace "artificial intelligence." However, whatever "intelligence" was deployed when signing the document appears to have failed at a critical moment.

Trump and six tech executives signed the second page of the agreement. The largest signature was, of course, Trump's—and beneath his characteristically angular name appeared an unexpected title:

Yes, the document signed by the president misspelled the name of the country as well:

Donald J. Trump, President of the United States of America

As of early Wednesday, the image with the misspelled country name remained on Trump's Truth Social account.

Although the agreement contains four voluntary steps for the tech industry to follow, it also hints that regulatory measures may be introduced in the future.
